title: FastAPI CRUD Endpoints: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on building CRUD endpoints in FastAPI: response models, PATCH partial updates, pagination, filtering and sorting, and 404 handling.

chapters.title: CRUD Endpoint Mental Model
points: CRUD maps to HTTP verbs: POST /items (create, 201), GET /items and GET /items/{id} (read, 200), PUT/PATCH /items/{id} (update, 200), DELETE /items/{id} (delete, 204)
Use plural nouns for resource paths and keep verbs out of URLs: /items, not /getItems
Use three schemas per resource: ItemCreate (input), ItemUpdate (all fields optional), ItemRead (output, includes id and server-set fields)
Path params identify one resource (/items/{id}); query params shape a collection (limit, filter, sort)
Keep the router thin: the endpoint validates input and calls a service or CRUD function that talks to the DB

chapters.title: Create, Read and Response Models
points: POST: @router.post('/items', response_model=ItemRead, status_code=201) returns the created object with its generated id
response_model filters the output: fields not in ItemRead (e.g. password_hash) never leave the API
Never reuse the DB model or the create schema as the response: input and output shapes differ
ORM objects need ItemRead with model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True) in Pydantic v2
Read-one: fetch by id, return the object; read-list: return list[ItemRead] with pagination params

chapters.title: Update: PUT vs PATCH and exclude_unset
points: PUT replaces the whole resource and requires all fields; PATCH changes only the fields sent
PATCH schema: every field Optional with default None (ItemUpdate)
data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True) keeps only fields the client actually sent
exclude_unset vs exclude_none: exclude_unset still allows an explicit null (clear a field); exclude_none drops it
Apply with for k, v in data.items(): setattr(obj, k, v), then commit and refresh
Plain model_dump() on a PATCH body writes None over every omitted field, which wipes data

chapters.title: Pagination: Limit/Offset vs Cursor
points: Limit/offset: ?limit=20&offset=40 maps to SQL LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40, simple and allows jumping to any page
Offset flaws: the DB scans and discards skipped rows (slow on deep pages), and inserts or deletes between requests cause duplicate or missing rows
Cursor (keyset): ?limit=20&cursor=<last_id> maps to WHERE id > :cursor ORDER BY id LIMIT 20, with constant cost at any depth and stable under inserts
Cursor response returns items plus next_cursor (null on the last page); fetch limit+1 rows to detect whether a next page exists
Validate with Query(20, ge=1, le=100) to cap limit; pagination needs a deterministic ORDER BY with a unique tiebreaker such as id

chapters.title: Filtering, Sorting and 404 Handling
points: Filters are optional query params: status: str | None = None, then add .where(...) only when the value is not None
Sort via ?sort=-created_at: a leading '-' means descending; whitelist allowed sort columns (dict or Literal) and never pass raw input into order_by
Constrain filter and sort values with Literal or Enum so FastAPI returns 422 on bad input automatically
Missing resource: obj = db.get(Item, id); if obj is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail='Item not found')
Apply the 404 check in read, update and delete; 404 means resource not found, 422 means invalid input, and an empty filtered list returns 200 with []

chapters.title: CRUD Endpoints Cheat Sheet
points: Status codes: POST 201, GET 200, PUT/PATCH 200, DELETE 204 (no body), missing 404, invalid 422
PATCH recipe: model_dump(exclude_unset=True), 404 check, setattr loop, commit, refresh
Pagination choice: offset for small admin tables and page jumps, cursor for feeds and large or changing data
Query param recipe: limit (ge=1, le=100), offset or cursor, whitelisted sort, optional filters
Checklist: separate Create/Update/Read schemas, response_model on every route, 404 on every by-id route
